name: Terra (Terraform Labs)
oneLiner: Built UST, a 'stablecoin' meant to always be worth $1, kept steady by code and its sister token LUNA instead of real dollars in a bank.
causeOfDeath: UST's $1 peg was held up by a 20% yield and a secret rescue; when big holders ran in May 2022, UST and LUNA spiralled to near zero.
moneyNote: Terraform Labs raised 'more than $200 million' from investors (Coinbase Ventures, Galaxy Digital and others). No reliable company valuation was published; LUNA and UST's combined market value lost was about $45 billion.
inOneMinute: Terra's UST was a **stablecoin** (a crypto coin meant to always equal $1) backed not by dollars but by an algorithm and its twin token, LUNA.
People piled in because a Terra app called Anchor paid **about 20% a year** on UST. In May 2022 the peg broke, and roughly **$45 billion** vanished in a week.
Founder Do Kwon fled, was caught in Montenegro with fake documents, **pleaded guilty to two fraud counts** in the US and got 15 years.
killerLine: A promise of stability **needs real reserves**, not clever code and confidence.

chapters.title: The idea: a dollar coin without dollars
chapters.body: Do Kwon and Daniel Shin started Terraform Labs in Seoul in January 2018. Their big product was UST, a stablecoin. Most stablecoins keep $1 in a bank for every coin. UST did not. Instead it was **'algorithmic'**: you could always swap 1 UST for $1 worth of LUNA, Terra's other token, and the other way round. If UST fell below $1, traders would buy it cheap and swap it for LUNA, pushing UST back up. In theory, code kept the price steady. In practice, it only worked **as long as people believed LUNA was worth something**. And LUNA was only worth something if people wanted UST.

chapters.title: The rise: 20% on your 'dollar'
chapters.body: To make people want UST, Terra launched Anchor, which paid **19.45% a year** on UST deposits — far more than any bank. Critics called it a giant Ponzi scheme, but money kept pouring in. LUNA hit an all-time high of $119.51 and briefly joined the top ten cryptocurrencies. The SEC later alleged Terra also misled investors by claiming a popular Korean payments app used its blockchain. It also alleged that in May 2021, when UST briefly fell below $1, Kwon told the world the algorithm had fixed it, while really **a third party had secretly bought UST** to rescue the peg. Investors learned the wrong lesson: that UST couldn't break.

chapters.title: The cracks: the reserve that melted
chapters.body: In 2022 the Luna Foundation Guard, set up to defend UST, bought bitcoin as a safety reserve. By 7 May 2022 it held **80,394 bitcoin, worth about $2.4 billion** — more than Tesla owned. On 9 May, UST started slipping below $1. The foundation sold its bitcoin to defend the peg. Within three days only 313 bitcoin were left. It was not enough. Every time UST holders swapped out, new LUNA was printed, so LUNA's price crashed, which made people trust UST even less. This feedback loop is called a **'death spiral'**. Within a week UST was worth about 10 cents.

chapters.title: The fall: from fugitive to prisoner
chapters.body: On 13 May 2022 Terraform halted the blockchain. LUNA fell to virtually zero. About $45 billion in market value was gone. South Korea issued an arrest warrant for Kwon in September 2022. In March 2023 he was **arrested in Montenegro while trying to fly to Dubai with falsified Costa Rican documents**. In April 2024 a US jury found Kwon and Terraform liable for fraud in the SEC's civil case, and they agreed to pay about $4.5 billion. Kwon was extradited to the US on 31 December 2024. In August 2025 he **pleaded guilty to two fraud counts**, and on 11 December 2025 he was sentenced to 15 years — more than the 12 years prosecutors asked for.

After pleading guilty to two fraud counts, Kwon is sentenced to 15 years.

mistakes.title: A 'stable' coin backed by its own twin
mistakes.explain: UST's value rested on LUNA, and LUNA's value rested on demand for UST. **Two things propping each other up is not a reserve.** When confidence cracked, the design guaranteed a death spiral instead of stopping one. A real reserve is something whose value doesn't depend on you, like cash or government bonds.

mistakes.title: Buying demand with a 20% yield
mistakes.explain: Anchor's 19.45% yield attracted deposits that existed only for the yield. **Money that comes for a subsidy leaves the moment it wobbles.** That's exactly what happened in May 2022. Anchor's high yield needed constant subsidy, so the demand it created was rented, not earned. A reward that the business cannot afford forever is a countdown timer.

mistakes.title: Hiding the 2021 rescue
mistakes.explain: The SEC alleged that when UST broke in May 2021, a third party secretly bought UST to restore the peg, while Kwon credited the algorithm. **Telling investors the system healed itself when someone propped it up** made the 2022 collapse far bigger.

mistakes.title: Misleading investors about real-world use
mistakes.explain: The SEC also alleged Terra falsely claimed a popular Korean payments app settled transactions on its blockchain, making LUNA look useful. **Fake adoption stories** are one of the most common crypto frauds. Investors should always ask partners directly whether a claimed integration is real.

warningSigns: Does your product only stay stable or valuable as long as new money keeps flowing in?
Are you paying users a yield or reward that your real business can't afford without fresh funding?
Have you ever fixed a crisis quietly and then told the public it fixed itself?
Do you claim partnerships or real-world usage that a partner would not confirm in writing?
Is your 'reserve' made mostly of your own token or something that falls when you do?

lessons.title: Stress-test your worst day
lessons.detail: Ask: what happens if 30% of users leave in 48 hours? If the honest answer is 'everything collapses', your design is the problem, not the market.

lessons.title: Subsidies buy users, not loyalty
lessons.detail: Cashback, high interest, free credits — they bring people in fast. Know how many would stay if you stopped tomorrow, and plan for that number.

lessons.title: Tell the truth about rescues
lessons.detail: If a partner or investor saves you in a crisis, disclose it. Hiding help makes people think you're stronger than you are, which makes the next crisis worse.

lessons.title: As a user, ask what backs a 'stable' thing
lessons.detail: Before you trust a stablecoin, wallet or savings app, ask what's held in reserve and who checks it. 'An algorithm' is not an answer.

lessons.title: As an investor, ask who is buying and why
lessons.detail: If most demand for a token or product comes from people chasing a reward the company pays for, that demand is rented, not real. Ask what happens to demand if the reward ends.

quote.text: It was simply a fraud propped up by a so-called algorithmic 'stablecoin'
quote.who: Gurbir S. Grewal, SEC Director of Enforcement
quote.context: Announcing fraud charges against Terraform Labs and Do Kwon, February 2023

afterlife.text: Terraform Labs filed for bankruptcy in January 2024 and agreed to wind down and hand remaining assets to investors and creditors. In June 2024 Terraform and Kwon agreed to pay the SEC about $4.5 billion. Kwon, sentenced in December 2025 to 15 years in the US, may also face trial in South Korea and could later seek a transfer there. In December 2024 Jump Trading's Tai Mo Shan paid $123 million to settle SEC claims that it misled investors about UST's stability. In February 2026 Terraform's bankruptcy administrator sued trading firm Jane Street, alleging insider trading during the collapse — an allegation, not a finding.
